cards.front: What is the side chain pKa of histidine, and why does that matter at physiological pH?
cards.back: ~6.0 — it is partially protonated at physiological pH, so it can shuttle protons in enzyme active sites
cards.citation: histidine has a side chain pKa near 6.0, so it is partially protonated at physiological pH and is the residue most often found in enzyme active sites that shuttle protons

cards.front: Which two amino acids carry a negatively charged side chain at physiological pH?
cards.citation:
At physiological pH, the acidic amino acids aspartate and glutamate carry a
negatively charged side chain.

cards.front: Structurally, what makes proline unique among the twenty amino acids?
cards.back: Its side chain bonds back to the backbone nitrogen, forming a rigid five-membered ring
cards.citation:
Proline is unique among the twenty amino acids in that its side chain bonds
back to the backbone nitrogen, forming a rigid five-membered ring.

cards.front: Why can't proline act as a hydrogen bond donor in a peptide?
cards.back: Once in a peptide bond, its ring nitrogen has no free hydrogen
cards.citation:
Because the
nitrogen lacks a free hydrogen once incorporated into a peptide bond, proline
cannot act as a hydrogen bond donor.

cards.front: Which residue has the greatest conformational freedom, and why?
cards.back: Glycine — its side chain is a single hydrogen atom
cards.citation:
Glycine, whose side chain is a single hydrogen atom, has the greatest
conformational freedom of any residue

cards.front: How do you calculate the pI of an amino acid with a nonionizable side chain?
cards.back: Average the two backbone pKa values (carboxyl and amino groups)
cards.citation:
For an amino acid with a nonionizable side chain, pI is the average of
the two backbone pKa values, that of the carboxyl group and that of the amino
group.

cards.front: For an amino acid with an ionizable side chain, which pKa values are averaged to get pI?
cards.back: The two pKa values that flank the neutral species
cards.citation:
For an amino acid with an ionizable side chain, pI is the average of
the two pKa values that flank the neutral species.

cards.front: What gives the peptide bond its partial double bond character?
cards.back: Resonance delocalization of the nitrogen lone pair into the carbonyl
cards.citation:
The peptide bond has partial double bond character arising from resonance
delocalization of the nitrogen lone pair into the carbonyl.

cards.front: Why is the trans configuration of the peptide bond strongly favored over cis?
cards.back: The cis arrangement puts the two alpha carbons in steric conflict
cards.citation:
The trans configuration is strongly favored over cis because the
cis arrangement places the two alpha carbons in steric conflict

cards.front: Which peptide bond is the exception to the strong preference for trans?
cards.back: The peptide bond preceding proline, where cis and trans are closer in energy
cards.citation:
the exception
is the peptide bond preceding proline, where cis and trans are closer in
energy
